config.title: Implement Mutable type

intro.title: Implement Mutable type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom TypeScript utility type called `Mutable`. This type will take an existing object type and make all its properties mutable (writable), removing any `readonly` modifiers. You will learn how to use mapped types with the `-readonly` modifier to transform type definitions. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system, including generics and mapped types. By the end, you'll understand how to create reusable type utilities that modify property mutability in a type-safe way.
intro.usecase: In real applications, you often need to work with data that can change after initialization. For example, in a dashboard with editable user profiles, the user data might start as readonly from an API but needs to become mutable when the user clicks 'Edit Profile'. The Mutable type utility lets you safely transform readonly types into editable ones, ensuring type safety while allowing necessary modifications in UI components like forms, settings panels, or interactive data tables.

objectives: Implement a Mutable type that removes readonly modifiers from object properties
Apply the Mutable type to transform existing readonly interfaces
Construct type definitions using mapped types with conditional modifiers
Manipulate type modifiers to control mutability in TypeScript
Integrate the Mutable type with existing type declarations
Configure type parameters to handle nested object structures
Initialize type transformations that preserve non-readonly properties

steps.title: Add readonly removal for arrays
steps.instruction: Extend the Mutable type to handle readonly arrays by removing the readonly modifier from array types.
steps.hint: You need to use a conditional type to check if the type is a readonly array, then return the mutable version.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Conditional type for arrays
type MakeMutable<T> = T extends readonly (infer U)[] ? U[] : T;

successCriteria: The Mutable type includes a conditional type that removes readonly from arrays.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your conditional type correctly removes readonly from arrays.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Try using a conditional type to check if T extends a readonly array.
